final.memo:
We have reached a juncture where the Company's slow-motion restructuring threatens the underlying value of its royalty assets. While management has acknowledged the need to divest commercial operations, their lack of a firm timetable and continued spending on unproven R&D candidates—evidenced by the recent clinical failure in ulcerative-colitis—indicate a management team prioritizing empire-building over shareholder returns [D03; D05].

Our original thesis was predicated on unlocking the value of the high-margin royalty stream by shedding the high-cost, low-return clinical operations [D07]. The current operating margin of -7.0% compared to peer benchmarks highlights an unacceptable drift that our capital cannot support [D06]. We are not in the business of waiting for internal committees to slowly prune the business while cash is consumed by research that lacks a clear path to commercial success [D05; D06].

We are escalating our involvement to demand an immediate, binding sale process for all remaining commercial assets. We expect the proceeds from these disposals to be returned to shareholders, not reinvested into a pipeline that has already demonstrated significant safety and efficacy risks [D03; D05]. It is time for a disciplined wind-down of the integrated entity to protect the core royalty economics from further tax leakage and overhead drag [D06].",
  "uncited_claims": []
}

drivers.driver: Management’s announced strategic review has been too slow, resulting in continued cash burn and persistent margin underperformance [D03; D06]
The clinical failure of the lead pipeline candidate demonstrates that the 'research' spending is an inefficient use of capital that threatens the royalty floor [D05]
As an active investor, our role is to accelerate the divestment of non-core assets to prevent value leakage from further organizational realignment [D07]
Existing royalty cash flows provide a clear valuation floor that is currently obscured by the company's consolidated operating loss [D03; D04]
